theorems.natural_language_statement:
Let two source arrays have lengths $N_L,N_R$, band size $g>0$, and stored residue buckets for modulus $p$ followed by global encoding modulus $p_h^J$, with right shift $\delta$. Put $K=\max\{\lceil N_L/g\rceil,\lceil N_R/g\rceil\}$, let $C$ be the number of occurrence vectors, and take source cutoff $c\le512hJ$.

Start the continuation in its specified frame, with the common count register equal to $K$. The source-pair data and exact cover tables precede the occurrence array; its $CJ$ cells end before bank header $b$. Assume the specified decoder and bank-batch procedures, the exact bank space and word budgets, $S\le W$, and $d+512hJ+14\le D$. The continuation terminates with
$$\mathrm{register}_0=b+5+K\sigma,$$
where $\sigma$ is the defined bank span. It stores the five-field header, all common-band source banks, and every occurrence row, preserving memory before the occurrence array.

This is the execution contract for the bank constructor after its count-selection branch.

$$r=\mathbf1_{m>0},\qquad \nu(o+2)=m,\qquad \nu(o+3)=C_0,$$

Let $f_0,\ldots,f_{n-1}$ be stored integers with $|f_j|\le U$, and let $g,p,m>0$ and $|\sigma|\le D$. Split the array into $K=0$ bands when $n=0$, otherwise $K=\lfloor(n-1)/g\rfloor+1$, each of length at most $g$. Assume the source ends before destination $b$, the installed band procedures and their residue workspace and word budgets fit, space fits in a word, and $d+5$ is below the depth limit. For each band $i$, the routine constructs a six-cell header, codes, histogram, and exact physical-position buckets for
$$
k_{i,j}=((f_{ig+j}\bmod p+\sigma)\bmod m),\qquad j<\min(g,n-ig).
$$
It returns $w=b+6K+K(3m+1+2\min(n,g))$, preserves memory below $b$, and meets the source-band setup time budget.

The retained fibers distinguish repeated source values by position.

A local destination table of capacity $\sum_{i=0}^{\min(b,V)}\binom Vi$ also ends below $z$.

$$\nu(\mathrm{dst}+\operatorname{rank}(T))=(-1)^{|T|}(Z_jf)(P\cup\iota T)(Z_jg)(Q\cup\iota T).$$
Execution takes the signed-leaf budget plus the width-$V$ address budget plus $90$, and preserves every other cell below $z$.

For any natural input size $n$, let $m$ be its binary logarithmic size, $h$ its prescribed micro-half, $J$ its block count, and $\mu$ its total micro-size. Assume the specified scale, local-parameter, global-size, square-root, and power procedures. The nineteen-cell destination ends before scratch $f$; the initializer's exact scratch and word budgets fit limits $S\le W$, and $d+512h+6\le D$.

The routine writes the parameter list $V(n)$ and returns the global radix:
$$\nu[\mathrm{dst},\mathrm{dst}+19)=V(n),\qquad r=p_h^J.$$
The list contains the five core scales; six local graph counts and threshold; the selected local prime $p_h$ and bucket cap; five global power, rounding, and band-size values; and the prime-window scale. It meets the sum of its component time budgets plus $400$ and preserves memory below $f$ outside the nineteen output cells.

This makes the construction's parameter header an executed result rather than assumed input data.

$$\kappa_j=((f(s+j)\bmod p)+\delta)\bmod m\qquad(j<t-s).$$
It preserves cells below this band's histogram except its six header cells. Its budget is
$$498\min(n,g)(\lfloor\log_2(U+1)\rfloor+\lfloor\log_2(p+\Delta+1)\rfloor+1)+233m+1333.$$

This completes one packed source band while protecting earlier retained bands.

Let $N$ be the length of the retained A-incidence list, and suppose a physical pair slot contains $(i,j)$ with $i<3N$, $j<(TM)^J$, and $i,j\le V$. Here $T$ is the local schedule length and $M$ the retained output-layer size. Assume exact stored A values, owners and positions, owner records, source-band pairs and banks, cover keys, shared reporting headers, and the layer-mask table. The owner selected by $i\bmod N$ has valid B and C band indices.

All retained inputs end before decoding base $e$, the occurrence table ends before its bank, $e+4+2J\le a$, and $a+20\le w$. Assume the decoder's stated space/word bounds, the source selector's individual address and scalar bounds, $S\le W$, $d+4<D$, and a word-bounded selected A value.

The fixed routine returns $a$ and stores
$$[i\bmod N,\lfloor i/N\rfloor,j,\operatorname{occurrenceCode}(j)]$$
plus the two decoded block rows at $e$, and the exact twenty-cell owner/source/catalog record at $a$. It preserves cells below $e$ and takes at most $J(200\lambda+700)+100\lambda+8880$ steps, where $\lambda=\lfloor\log_2(V+1)\rfloor$.

This connects an emitted pair slot to its retained reporting inputs.

$$
r=|B||C|+|A||B|+|A||C|.

Let $n$ stored masks satisfy $m_i<2^L$, and let $R$ stored coefficient pairs $w^0_j,w^1_j$ have natural entries at most $U$. Masks and coefficient rows end by destination $z$, the $Rn$-cell output ends by reusable scratch $f$, and the local-row space and full word budgets fit the machine limits. Assume space fits in a word and $d+L+3$ fits in the depth limit. The installed routines produce
$$
\mu'(z+jn+i)=\sum_{a<L:\,\operatorname{bit}(m_i,a)=0}
\bigl(w^1_j(a)-w^0_j(a)\bigr)
\quad(j<R,\ i<n).
$$
They preserve memory below $z$ and use $R(\operatorname{rowTime}(L,n)+\operatorname{copyTime}(n)+130)+20$ steps.

This creates the complete occurrence-by-output array of signed local keys.

Let $m=2^k$ and let integer coefficient lists $A,B$ each have length $2m$ and coefficients bounded in absolute value by $U$. Their memory segments and the $4m$-cell output end by scratch base $f$. Assume $f+16m$ fits in space, $128(2m)^3(U+1)^2$ fits in a word, space fits in a word, and $d$ is below the depth limit. Suppose every size-$m$ recursive call at depth $d+1$ satisfies the stated multiplication contract under its own layout and word bounds. Then the recursive body yields
$$
\mu'(z+j)=[X^j](A(X)B(X))\quad(j<4m)
$$
within $T(k+1)-4$ steps, where $T(0)=30$ and $T(k+1)=3T(k)+2500\,2^k$. Below $f$, only the output may change.

Let $T,M\ge1$, $k\le V$, and let a stored mask table $f(s)$ for $s<M$ have natural values at most $U$. Set $b_j=\lfloor k/(TM)^{J-1-j}\rfloor\bmod(TM)$ for $j<J$. The mask table ends before output base $a$, $a+2J\le w$, and assume
$$w+\lfloor\log_2(V+1)\rfloor+2\le S\le B,\quad d+2<D,$$
$$32(V+TM+T+M+J+T^J+U+10)\le B.$$
For the specified digit, step, and division procedures, the decoder writes
$$\nu(a+j)=\lfloor b_j/M\rfloor,\qquad\nu(a+J+j)=f(b_j\bmod M),$$
and returns $\sum_{j<J}\lfloor b_j/M\rfloor T^{J-1-j}$. Its budget is $J(200\lfloor\log_2(V+1)\rfloor+700)+130$, and cells below $a$ are preserved.

This separates each fixed-width local-record digit into its occurrence index and retained mask, in original block order.

theorems.natural_language_statement:
Consider $J$ bit rows of length $L$, a required weight $h\le L$, and a positive modulus $p$. Each row selects one of $M$ pairs of weight rows, whose entries are at most $U$; that selection chooses one of $K$ left and right histograms, bounded by $V$. Assume memory stores these arrays exactly, all selection indices are valid, and all bits are Boolean. Their reserved intervals end before the two-cell row-result buffer at $r$; the final two-cell output ends by $r$, and scratch starts at $f\ge r+2$. Require $S\le W$, $d+1<D$, $f+\lfloor\log_2(LU+1)\rfloor+5\le S$, and $(L+1)(U+1)+4LU+4p+2L+V+\mathrm{cap}+19\le W$.

Let $F_j^\ell,F_j^r$ be the row flags: the row has $h$ ones and its corresponding residue bucket contains at most $\mathrm{cap}$ elements, with the two weight rows interchanged for the right flag. The specified procedures write
$$\nu(a)=\prod_{j<J}F_j^\ell,\qquad\nu(a+1)=\prod_{j<J}F_j^r.$$
They take at most $J(150L+2R_{LU}+560)+100$ steps, where $R_z=43(\lfloor\log_2(z+1)\rfloor+1)+34$, and preserve memory below $r$ outside the output.

The products implement simultaneous acceptance over every block.

Let a stored $r\times c$ matrix $A$ have entries in $\{0,1\}$ and $r>0$. Starting with all $c$ columns active, choose at each round the least row index maximizing the number of active columns it covers, then deactivate those covered columns. Let $g_0,\ldots,g_{t-1}$ and $U_t$ be the resulting choices and remaining active set.

Assume the specified fill, score-selection, and update procedures. The source matrix ends before scratch base $a$, and
$$a+c+r+t\le S\le B,\quad1\le B,\quad d+2<D.$$
The routine returns $o=a+c+r$ and writes
$$\nu(o+i)=g_i\ (i<t),\qquad\nu(a+j)=\mathbf1_{j\in U_t}\ (j<c).$$
It preserves every cell outside $[a,a+c+r+t)$ and terminates within
$$13c+106+t(32rc+122r+26c+300)$$
steps.

This realizes the precise finite greedy schedule, including its tie-breaking and repeated choices.

Let a source segment have length $n$, band width $g>0$, and owner label $o$. A record has flag $f$ and band index $a$; require $a<\lceil n/g\rceil$ whenever $f=1$. Put $s=ag$ and let $m=\min(g,n-s)$ if $f=1$, otherwise $m=0$. Let $v,o_0,z$ be bases of three output arrays of capacity $C$, with previous length $t$ and $t+m\le C$. Assume
$$\mathrm{src}+n\le v,\quad v+C\le o_0,\quad o_0+C\le z,\quad z+C\le S\le B,$$
$ n+g+o+10\le B$ and $d+1<D$. For the specified append, row-copy, and fill procedures, the call returns $t+m$ within $59g+362$ steps and writes, for $j<m$,
$$\bigl(\nu(v+t+j),\nu(o_0+t+j),\nu(z+t+j)\bigr)=\bigl(\mu(\mathrm{src}+s+j),o,s+j\bigr).$$
All other cells are preserved.
